root_idea.summary: A principle of gathering or compacting something while its parts remain distinguishable or discontinuous.
root_idea.development: This orientation appears in clotted wool and hair, broken-up cloud formations, elevated ground beside hollows, and raised parts of the back. Related extensions include the clustering of ticks and the stillness associated with their removal.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the singular classical citation form قِرْدٌ; the supplied Quranic form is the plural قِرَدَة.

senses.definition: An ape, monkey, or baboon; plural قِرَدَةٌ.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrences use the plural form قِرَدَةٌ. In the passages describing people being made into apes, the reported interpretation varies between a transformation of visible form and a transformation of character to resemble that of apes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of wool or hair: to fall off gradually, become compacted into clumps, or become knotted at the ends.
Of a tanned skin: to become worm-eaten.
To become silent through inability to speak, or to become still, abject, humble, or submissive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The figurative associations are explained through the stillness of a camel while ticks are removed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To collect or acquire for one's family; specifically, to collect clarified butter or milk in a skin.
To remove or pluck ticks from an animal, especially a camel.
To render submissive or tractable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested especially of a camel after its ticks have been removed; the related intransitive use describes the camel becoming submissive or tractable.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To beguile, wheedle, or cajole someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of approaching or handling someone gently in order to overcome resistance, sometimes with deceptive intent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel: to become still, quiet, or tranquil after its ticks have been removed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can also describe moving at a gentle pace without shaking or jolting the rider.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become silent, still, quiet, or submissive; also, to feign being dead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This figurative use is applied to a person as well as to stillness generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cling to the ground through abjectness or submissiveness.
Of flour: to become heaped, with one part lying upon another.
A حَوْدَل, in the conventional expression ابن القرد.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized lexical expression rather than the ordinary animal sense of قِرْدٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Refuse of wool and other soft hair or fiber; especially material that falls off gradually and becomes compacted or clotted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A piece of this material is قَرَدَةٌ. The term also occurs in a proverb applied to someone who postpones a necessary task until it becomes difficult.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Palm branches stripped of their leaves.
A down-like or fiber-like substance adhering to the plant called طُرْثُوث.
Small detached cloudlets or little scattered collections of cloud.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The formations are described as smaller than ordinary clouds and not joined into one mass.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hesitation in speech.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meaning is connected with leaving part of what one intends to say unspoken.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wool or hair that has contracted together, become compacted into lumps, and knotted at its extremities.
A cloud formation broken into portions or layers that are compacted together one upon another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description includes disjoined or irregular masses resembling compacted soft hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse compact and firm in frame, not lax.
Of a camel or similar animal: abounding in ticks.
Accumulated foam cast from a camel's mouth.
Elevated, rugged, or prominent ground, especially ground rising beside a hollow or depressed place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can also refer to an even or plain tract and to an extended strip of ground, according to the cited lexical descriptions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The uppermost or raised part of the back of a beast of burden, especially the withers.
The severity, sharpness, or sterile severity of winter.
A tick, an insect that clings to camels and similar animals and bites them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The collective plural is قِرْدَانٌ; the word may also refer collectively to ticks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The nipple of the breast or udder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative designation based on the resemblance of a nipple to a large tick.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place between the fetlock and hoof of a horse, or between the phalanges of a camel's foot.
A camel that does not impatiently avoid having its ticks plucked off.
A still or quiet man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of the camel description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A trainer of an ape, monkey, or baboon.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer-only cross-reference to قَرَدٌ and قَرِدٌ.

cautions: The displayed Quranic headword is the singular قِرْدٌ, while all three supplied Quran occurrences are the plural قِرَدَةٌ.
The interpretation of the Quranic transformation passages is reported in two ways: physical resemblance to apes or resemblance in character without physical transformation.
